# Rounding to nearest

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `to_nearest_2` · proved for finite operands · **UNVERIFIED** for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$x$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(x).$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to_nearest(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `T` |  |
| `Expansion<T, 1>(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | explicit: the leading limb |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(x)$: the number of the format nearest to $x$, ties to even.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `to_nearest_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Convert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Convert.v), against `to_nearest_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition to_nearest_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  let t := to_nearest_2 x0 x1 in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RN emin prec (x0 + x1).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $x$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.

and then:

- If every operand is finite: $t = \mathrm{RN}(x)$, the nearest number of `T` with ties to even, or $\pm\infty$ when $\lvert x\rvert \ge \Omega + \tfrac12\,\mathrm{ulp}(\Omega)$ ($\Omega$ is the largest finite number of `T`).
- If an operand is infinite or NaN: $t = x_0$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement: UNVERIFIED.** No proof of it is checked (`ieee_status` is `unverified` in `gen/claims.json`). The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/to_nearest_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/to_nearest_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# RN(x) of a 2-limb number: x0 itself, since a normalized x has x0 = RN(x0 + x1).

t = copy(x0)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#to_nearest_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the statement on finite operands; the stored summaries hold no measurement of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 62 400 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 62 400 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 9 337 519 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
- Anything about infinite and NaN operands, as a guarantee: that statement is a target until its proof is checked.
